findings.title: Backup codes are not consumed when disabling 2FA and are not rate limited

response:
## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security
Title: Backup codes are not consumed when disabling 2FA and are not rate limited

Affected:
- apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:47-66

Explanation:
The backup code branch only validates the code. It relies on the later update that nulls `backupCodes`. If that update fails, the code stays valid. More importantly, the backup code path adds a brute-force surface with no rate limiting. Codes are 40 bits of entropy, so this is hard to guess, but the endpoint should still be limited, as login is via `checkRateLimitAndThrowError`. The comparison uses `indexOf`, which is not constant-time. `JSON.parse` of the decrypted data is not guarded. A non-string `req.body.backupCode` makes `replaceAll` throw and return a 500.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
if (typeof req.body.backupCode !== "string") return res.status(400).json({ error: ErrorCode.IncorrectBackupCode });
// add rate limiting for this endpoint, and validate the input type before calling replaceAll
~~~

## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug
Title: Backup codes are written to the DB before 2FA is confirmed, and an unvalidated code type can throw at login

Affected:
- apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:60-71
- packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131-156

Explanation:
`setup` overwrites `backupCodes` for a user whose 2FA is already enabled, and it can only run for a user who has 2FA disabled. A repeated setup call replaces the codes before the TOTP is verified. At login, `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll` assumes a string. Used codes are set to `null` in the array, and the stored array is still compared with `indexOf`. A submitted empty string cannot match null, so this is fine. Concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed, because there is no atomic compare-and-update (a race), so the code is not strictly single-use.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// use a conditional update (updateMany where backupCodes = old ciphertext) and check count === 1 before letting the login proceed
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Backup-code form field remains registered and required across toggles, and the disable flow sends stale values

Affected:
- apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:17-26
- apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:103-121

Explanation:
The "Lost access" button in the disable modal has no `type="button"`, so it may submit the form. The `Button` default type is likely "button", but this depends on code outside the diff. `resetForm` also sets `totpCode` to "" while the 6-digit TwoFactor component keeps its own internal state. After toggling, the TwoFactor UI can show stale digits while the form value is empty. In the disable API, `backupCode` is sent as "" when TOTP is used, which is falsy, so this works. The login `formSchema` may not include `backupCode`, which could strip the field under the zod resolver; this cannot be verified from the diff.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
<Button type="button" color="minimal" ...>
// ensure formSchema allows backupCode
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Closing the enable dialog with the backup code step open loses the codes and state

Affected:
- apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:222-231
- apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:266-270

Explanation:
2FA is already enabled when the backup codes step is shown. Dismissing the dialog via Escape or the overlay (`onOpenChange`) does not reset the state, and the user may never see the codes. The step stays at `DisplayBackupCodes` on the next open. `onEnable` is also not called in that case. The `backupCodesUrl` blob is never revoked on close or unmount, which leaks it. `useState([])` is typed `never[]`, so TypeScript may complain about `backupCodes.map`.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const [backupCodes, setBackupCodes] = useState<string[]>([]);
// handle onOpenChange(false) at the backup step by calling resetState() and onEnable(), and revoke the URL on close
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Component name mismatch and unused password type

Affected:
- apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:7
- apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:174-176

Explanation:
`BackupCode.tsx` exports a component named `TwoFactor`, which is confusing in stack traces and devtools. `PasswordField` is given a redundant `type="password"`, which may conflict with the visibility toggle. If the prop is spread after the internal `type`, the toggle would stop working.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
export default function BackupCode({ center = true }) {
// remove type="password" from PasswordField
~~~
